facilities.name: Centipedegrass lawn tile
notes: Default unimproved lawn is centipedegrass.
Natural sunlight, rainfall, temperature, and ordinary soil conditions are abstracted.
Scat up to the assimilation capacity is treated as passively incorporated into the soil.

facilities.name: Chicken coop
notes: Static shelter/roosting facility for free-ranging laying hens.
Feed, water, eggs, scat, and variable labor scale with current chicken count.
Current fill level is runtime state, not part of the facility type definition.

facilities.name: Compost pile

active_compost.notes: Pre-composted material bypasses fresh-feedstock balancing and enters the active-compost pool directly.

notes: All material pools share the 500 lb physical capacity.
Kitchen waste creates a nominal carbonaceous plant waste demand of 0.5 lb per lb; avian scat creates a demand of 1.5 lb per lb.
During servicing, balanced nitrogen-rich inputs and carbonaceous plant waste are mixed into generic feedstock.
Each hour mature conversion is processed first, then fresh feedstock conversion. Nominal daily conversion fractions are compounded to hourly rates.

Feedstock retains 70% of processed mass as active compost; active compost retains 65% as mature soil amendment. The remainder represents water loss, carbon dioxide, and other untracked biological losses.
Mature compost remains physically at the pile until the Homesteader collects it.
BSFL pre-compost or other active-compost material can be added directly to the active-compost pool and does not create a carbon-balancing requirement.

facilities.name: BSFL reactor
notes: Physical bin dimensions are approximately 4 ft x 4 ft x 2.5 ft (about 40 ft3 gross volume).

Working surface is approximately 16 ft2; only a shallow active substrate layer is assumed so most gross volume remains available for ventilation, heat dissipation, drainage, and self-harvest geometry.
Usable feedstock capacity is 60 lb and maximum standing larval biomass is 20 lb.
At maximum larval biomass, nominal feed-processing capacity is 26 lb/day (20 lb larvae x 1.3 lb feed/lb larvae/day).
Of processed feed, nominal mass balance is 35% new larval biomass, 35% frass/pre-compost residue, and 30% untracked metabolic, gaseous, and evaporative losses.
Larval growth is additionally capped at 0.45 of standing biomass per day; the 1.3 feed rate and 0.35 yield were intentionally chosen to closely match that ceiling.
Self-harvest is modeled as 0.08 of standing larval biomass per day, scaled by feeding activity; no feed means no modeled growth or maturation loss.
Routine reactor tending accrues 0.1 labor-hours/day; collection and transport of feedstocks are accounted for elsewhere.
Frass, moultings, and indigestible residue are treated as active compost (BSFL pre-compost) and remain at the reactor until collected.

facilities.name: Electrosolar array
notes: Sunlight and weather inputs are abstracted for the initial model.
Average output is annualized; time-of-day and weather variation can be added later.
Rated capacity is stored separately so later production logic can use environmental modifiers.

facilities.name: Rain barrel
notes: Catchment is abstracted as approximately 10 ft x 10 ft of roof.
Intermittent rainfall is not yet modeled; 10 gal/day is the annualized average inflow.

facilities.name: In-ground garden plot
notes: Crop-dependent inputs, outputs, labor, and production rates are intentionally deferred.
Garden behavior will be defined through a later planting/crop layer.
